newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico primary Cetes rates rise on U.S. rate hikes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico primary Cetes rates rise on U.S. rate hikes.

text.p: Mexico's primary Cetes rates rose across the yield curve on Tuesday as concerns grew over rising interest rates in the United States, analysts said.
Demand fell sharply at Banco de Mexico's weekly treasury bill auction, particularly for the bellwether one-month paper.

"It's an internal reaction to external factors," Santander Investment economist Hector Chavez told Reuters. "Investors are looking for a better yield to stay here to make up for the opportunity cost."
The one-month Cetes rate rose a sharp 127 basis points to 21.86 percent, a higher-than-expected increase.
A survey by Reuters of nine money market dealers earlier in the day found expectations of a rise of 63 basis points in the bellwether one-month rate.
A survey by MMS International found expectations of a rise in the one-month rate to between 21.0 percent and 21.4 percent.
Market players have been concerned that the U.S. Federal Reserve could increase the federal funds rate again in May after lifting the key rate by 25 basis points in March.
Nationsbank analyst Luis Cedeno said the rise in Mexican rates "makes the market more attractive while short-term rates in the United States are rising and the stock market is dropping".
The rate on the U.S. long bond has also risen sharply, touching 7.08 percent on Tuesday.
Mexican one-month Cetes rates have been on a roller-coaster ride in the past few weeks, rising 458 basis points in early March.
But rates fell in the last two auctions, resuming a downward trend starting late last year that brought Mexican interest rates to their lowest levels since the 1994 peso crash.
Investors were cheered by dwindling inflationary pressures in Mexico and a growing economy.
Although concerns over higher interest rates in the U.S. caused the upward blip earlier last month, a deepening sense of confidence in Mexico's economy helped contain those increases, analysts said.

"In general, solid Mexican fundamentals -- prospects for declining monthly inflation, healthy growth and continued external balance -- are allowing the local bond and currency markets to weather the current uncertainty in U.S. financial markets," brokerage Valores Finamex said in a report on Tuesday.
Still, demand fell this week, dropping to 9.81 billion pesos compared to 15.05 billion pesos last week. There were 3.0 billion pesos worth of Cetes on offer.
Demand for the one-month paper fell sharply to 1.146 billion pesos for the 800 million pesos on offer.
That compares to the 2.97 billion pesos demanded for the 800 million pesos worth of one-month paper on offer last week.
